Impede

/im-PEED/ - rhymes with speed · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Impede means to slow or obstruct the progress of something.

Fog impeded the search all night without ever ending it; the boats simply moved at a crawl between calls.

Worked Example

Halfway across the Atlantic, the clipper's log begins complaining about weed. Barnacles by the thousand had settled along her hull, each one a knuckle of drag, and the same wind that had driven her nine knots in April now managed barely six. Nothing was broken. Nothing was blocked. The ship was simply towing a reef of passengers the rest of the way to port.

Impede is the exact word for what the barnacles did, because to impede is to slow or obstruct the progress of something — the voyage continues, dragging. A paralyzed ship would sit dead in the water, and a delayed one merely arrives late; impede names the friction itself, the going made heavy while the going goes on.

How Impede Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bog down

bog down: the mud picture — progress that labors on under the weight

obstruct

obstruct: puts a thing in the path; impede covers any drag, obstacle or none

Antonyms

hasten

hasten: clears the road and quickens the pace

ease

ease: takes the friction out of the going

How Strong Is It? — delay → impede → paralyze

delay vs. impede

delay vs. impede: Delay is the mildest verdict — the shipment still arrives whole, just later than the paper promised.

paralyze vs. impede

paralyze vs. impede: Paralyze goes further than impede — impeded traffic still crawls forward; paralyzed traffic stands dead where it is.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im-

Prefix — im-: in, into

Root — ped

Root — ped: foot (Latin pes, pedis)

Put it together

Put it together: Im- (in) + ped (foot) = to catch by the feet. Latin impedire meant to shackle or hobble — feet in the trap — and the picture survives every modern use: what impedes you does not stop you; it makes you walk as if in leg irons.

Use the root in a new word: pedestrian

Use the root in a new word: pedestrian: A pedestrian is simply the person on foot — Latin ped- doing its plainest daily work on every crosswalk sign.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Impede is the engineer's and referee's verb: progress continues, slower. If movement stops outright, you want halt or paralyze; if someone is bodily held, that is this unit's restrain; and repress is heavier still — force from above holding a thing down. Impede judges nobody. It just measures the drag.
